title: docs: explain agents and MCP architecture
author: Circuit-Overtime
pr_body_excerpt:
- Documents current prompt-agent and endpoint-agent request boundaries, `ag_` run-token security, hosted MCP routing, and billing.
- Adds sequence diagrams for user-to-agent-to-model, agent-to-MCP, and delegated billing flows.
- Separates shipped behavior from the open restriction, delegation, endpoint-MCP verification, and hosting work.
- Records the accepted direction and unresolved runtime decisions from #13657 without committing to untested infrastructure.
- Links the guide from `DEVELOP.md`.

Fixes #14169
Related: #13657

gist.headline: A map for the agents
gist.blurb: The agent garden has a proper trail map now. Follow a request from user to model to MCP server, with the billing pollen and run tokens labeled along the way.
gist.summary: Added AGENTS_AND_MCP.md documenting prompt-agent and endpoint-agent boundaries, ag_ run-token security, hosted MCP routing, delegated billing, and the still-open runtime decisions from #13657.
gist.impact: Developers can now trace user-to-agent-to-model and agent-to-MCP flows through sequence diagrams, while clearly seeing which MCP architecture behavior is already shipped versus still being designed.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy architecture map for the agent system: Polli acts as a tiny trail guide, following labeled paths between a user terminal, a prompt-agent garden shed, an endpoint-agent signpost, a hosted MCP bridge, and a glowing model server. Small ag_ token fireflies travel safely along the route, while flowers and code-plants make the technical diagram feel like an inviting garden map.
